what_happened: The job added a decision-brief renderer with refusal checks to `xtask site`. The verifier rejected it at the final verdict with three major findings and no listed unmet criteria or failed checks. (1) Briefs are read from a new file format that nothing writes, and the real waiting Steward proposals are never read. On the real repository the decisions page would always say "Nothing is waiting". (2) The record links are relative paths that will not open on the published site, so "every claim links to its record" is not met in practice. (3) A Steward-proposal brief is fixed text. Every proposal gets the recommendation "Approve" and the same cost, risk and reason, each linked to a record that does not say so. The refusal checks and renderer probably exist and pass on hand-made input. The work does not do the job on real data.
cause: The acceptance criteria and tests checked that the renderer, its refusal rules and the brief type exist and behave on fixtures the job wrote itself. Nothing required the output to be produced from the repository's real inputs, such as the actual Steward proposal records, or the links to be checked as resolvable on the published site. A producer can therefore invent a new input format and fixed placeholder content, pass every check, and be caught only when the verifier compares the page with the real repository. Nothing at the plan or critic stage asks where the real data comes from and who writes it.
prevention: For any job that renders or reports from repository records, require two things at plan and criteria stage. First, each criterion must be demonstrated by running the real command on the real (or a copied snapshot of the) repository and asserting content that came from the actual records, such as a known waiting proposal's own title, recommendation and cost. A fixture the job invented does not count. Second, the plan must name the existing writer of every input it reads, and the critic must reject any new input format that nothing writes. For site output, links must be checked to resolve against the published base path.
proposed_request: Redo the decision-brief page in `xtask site` so it works on the real repository. Outcome: the decisions page lists every Steward proposal that is actually waiting for the owner, read from the records Athena already writes for proposals. Do not add a new brief file format that nothing writes. For each proposal the brief shows that proposal's own title, recommendation, cost, risk and reason, taken from its record, and refuses to render (with a clear message) any brief where one of these is missing or the recommendation is not supported by the record. Every claim links to its record using a link that opens on the published site (correct base path, not a bare relative path from the page). Acceptance: (1) running `xtask site` on a snapshot of the real repository that holds at least one waiting proposal produces a decisions page naming that proposal and its own recommendation, cost, risk and reason, and not 'Nothing is waiting'; (2) a test with two proposals that have different recommendations and costs shows each brief carries its own values; (3) a test checks that every record link in the generated page resolves to an existing generated file or record under the site's published base path; (4) the refusal checks have a test each for a missing field and an unsupported recommendation; (5) with no waiting proposals the page says nothing is waiting; (6) fmt, clippy and the full test suite pass, and the CHANGELOG has an entry. Reuse the existing proposal-reading code if there is any, and say in the report which existing code was reused.
